title: How many whole units are in each of three fractions?
description: Each fraction is split into groups of its bottom number that make whole units, with a few parts left over. The board counts the groups in all three fractions and checks by putting the pieces back together.
teaching_notes: One idea: take out as many groups of the bottom number as fit in the top number. Watch for students who count the leftover parts as another whole.

source: Figure it Out Q1 (section 7.5, second block)
video_script.why: A learner finds the whole units in fractions greater than one by taking out groups of the bottom number.
video_script.substitution: the book's own fractions eight thirds, eleven fifths and nine fourths
video_script.anchor: three rows of equal part bars for eight thirds, eleven fifths and nine fourths
video_script.payoff_line: Each of the three fractions has two whole units

final_answer.spoken: each of the three fractions has two whole units

video_script.fraction_reading: three thirds, eight thirds, five fifths, eleven fifths, four fourths, nine fourths
maths_rules: 3 thirds, 5 fifths or 4 fourths make 1 whole
8/3 = 6/3 + 2/3 and 6 thirds = 2 groups of 3 thirds = 2 wholes
11/5 = 10/5 + 1/5 and 10 fifths = 2 groups of 5 fifths = 2 wholes
9/4 = 8/4 + 1/4 and 8 fourths = 2 groups of 4 fourths = 2 wholes
video_script.design: Three rows of part bars. In each row the parts join in groups of the bottom number into two whole bars, and a few parts stay alone.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; three fractions 8/3, 11/5 and 9/4, each with a row of equal part bars

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.rows: three rows of part bars appear, one for each fraction
marks.ask: the question is written beside the rows

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it is about three fractions.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>The fractions are eight thirds, eleven fifths and nine fourths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many whole units are there in each of them?

beats.on_screen: the three rows stay; the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a whole unit bar beside three third bars, five fifth bars and four fourth bars of the same length

marks.need: a whole unit bar appears next to a row of equal parts that fill it
marks.fill: three thirds, five fifths and four fourths are shown filling one whole unit

narration: <bookmark mark='need'/>A whole unit needs as many parts as the bottom number says.
<bookmark mark='fill'/>Three thirds, five fifths or four fourths each fill one whole unit.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the fractions that we have to look at are eight thirds, eleven fifths and nine fourths.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many whole units are in each fraction
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many whole units are in each of them.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 8/3 = 6/3 + 2/3; 6 thirds = 2 groups of 3 thirds = 2 wholes

marks.split: eight thirds is split into six thirds and two thirds
marks.groups: the six thirds join in groups of three into two whole bars

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, we use the same way as the examples in your book. Eight thirds is six thirds and two thirds.
<bookmark mark='groups'/>Six thirds make two groups of three thirds, so there are two whole units.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 11/5 = 10/5 + 1/5; 10 fifths = 2 groups of 5 fifths = 2 wholes

marks.split: eleven fifths is split into ten fifths and one fifth
marks.groups: the ten fifths join in groups of five into two whole bars

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step two, eleven fifths is ten fifths and one fifth.
<bookmark mark='groups'/>Ten fifths make two groups of five fifths, so there are two whole units.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 9/4 = 8/4 + 1/4; 8 fourths = 2 groups of 4 fourths = 2 wholes

marks.split: nine fourths is split into eight fourths and one fourth
marks.groups: the eight fourths join in groups of four into two whole bars

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step three, nine fourths is eight fourths and one fourth.
<bookmark mark='groups'/>Eight fourths make two groups of four fourths, so there are two whole units again.

marks.one: the two wholes and the two leftover thirds are put back together as eight thirds
marks.two: the other two fractions are put back together in the same way

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>To check, put the pieces back together. Two groups of three thirds and two thirds make eight thirds.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Two groups of five fifths and one fifth make eleven fifths. Two groups of four fourths and one fourth make nine fourths.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Each of the three fractions has two whole units.
The leftover parts are two thirds, one fifth and one fourth.
